title: AVI-HT: Adaptive Vision-IMU Fusion for 3D Gloved Hand Tracking
claim: Fusing a second sensing modality keeps predictions aligned with ground truth through occlusion, where the single-modality baseline drifts.
layout: Left capture-setup column, right frame strip over error-vs-time plot with zoom callout
description: The figure has two parts. The left column shows the capture setup. A cartoon of a person in a VR-style headset and a sensing glove sits at a desk, labeled 'Egocentric Cameras'. Below it is a photo of the blue glove with its IMU modules exploded out, labeled 'Data Sensing Glove' and '6-DoF IMU'. The right side has a legend: green is ground truth, blue is AVI-HT (vision plus IMU), and red is UMETrack (vision only). A gray callout holds six grayscale egocentric frames of a hand moving a notebook. Under each frame is a 3D hand mesh with the three colors overlaid. A line plot of keypoint error (mm) against temporal index sits below. The red line (vision-only) rises above the blue line (ours) inside a shaded window that links to the frames. The eye goes first to the colored meshes.
caption: 3D hand tracking from egocentric vision and on-glove IMUs. (Left) Our multi-modal data capture setup that consists of an egocentric camera and a data sensing glove with 12 6-DoF IMU sensors. (Right) Qualitative comparison on 4 egocentric frames. For each frame, the top row shows an inset hand diagram. The bottom row shows the corresponding 3D hand pose tracking overlaid for UMETrack and AVI-HT against ground truth. The tracking results by AVI-HT are closely aligned with the ground truth, while the vision-only baseline deviates substantially. The top yellow patches highlight the activated IMU sensors by the adaptive attention module of AVI-HT, indicating the regions with greater reliance on IMU signals over egocentric vision. Best viewed in color.
abstract: We present AVI-HT, an adaptive visual-IMU fusion approach for tracking 3D hand poses by jointly modeling the egocentric images with on-glove 6-DoF IMU signals. AVI-HT significantly improved accuracy and availability, particularly in hand-object interaction (HOI) scenarios involving heavy visual occlusion. Two complementary ingredients underpin its success: (1) synchronized multi-modal training data pairing on-body vision-IMU sensor streams with ground-truth 3D hand poses from a motion-capture system, and (2) a cross-sensor deep attention mechanism that adaptively modulates the trust assigned to the vision and individual IMU sensors. To evaluate AVI-HT in real-world settings, we conduct extensive experiments on our DexGloveHOI dataset that consists of 100K+ pairwise vision-IMU samples with synchronized 3D annotated poses, in which users manipulate a variety of objects during daily tasks. We compare against multiple single- and multi-modal tracking approaches under two hand models (UmeTrack, MANO). The results show that AVI-HT reduces mean keypoint error by 16.1% and its wrist-aligned variant by 24.2% over the baselines. A hand-object contact evaluation shows that AVI-HT keeps finger contacts with the manipulated object more accurately and consistently over time, reducing contact losses by 8.5%. Ablation studies further show that our fusion design outperforms simpler schemes and that the gains grow with occlusion and hold across subjects.
